primaryText: Storks have a favorite nesting area.
comment: p. 337: generics in transparent contexts exhibit the usual scope ambiguities, after Schubert and Pelletier 1989; p. 346 derives both readings. narrow: there is a favorite nesting area x such that, in general, storks nest in x. wide: in general, a stork has a favorite nesting area.

p. 338: bad because it can only get the implausible reading, one cigarette that John habitually smokes (narrow), not the plausible one, John habitually in a situation where there is a cigarette he smokes (wide); fn. 4: focus does not help. Same sentence as (45a) p. 349 with Mary.

primaryText: John smokes a brand of French cigarette.
comment: p. 338: habituals without any restriction take narrow scope only (after Krifka et al. 1995); in (17b) too the habitual takes narrow scope, and one brand that John habitually smokes makes sense.

primaryText: John needed but didn't buy a new coat.
comment: p. 341: can only mean (25b), John didn't buy any new coat, with negation over the type-shifted buy (narrow), not (25c), there is a new coat John didn't buy (wide); fn. 10: (25c) is available when need is read de re, with no type mismatch.
